extracted.intended_audience: students, coaches, and organizers of the Iranian Mathematical Olympiad; problem solvers seeking Iran MO problems
extracted.subtask_description: A webpage listing Iranian Mathematical Olympiad problems by year and describing the competition structure, rounds, selection numbers, and training/selection program used to pick the IMO team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary round format
rubrics_metrics.description: The preliminary round consists of 30 multiple choice questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referred to as the first round (preliminary). This round is used to reduce the field before inviting students to the training camp/second round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of subsequent rounds (IMO format)
rubrics_metrics.description: The other three rounds are nowadays held in the IMO format each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rounds after the preliminary follow the International Mathematical Olympiad style (proof-based problems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-first-round selection size
rubrics_metrics.description: After the first round 40 students are invited for a training camp and the second round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first-round cutoff is typically set to invite 40 students to the next stage/training camp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification for IMO training camp and third round
rubrics_metrics.description: Twelve of them qualify for the IMO training camp and the third round of the national MO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the training camp/second round cohort, 12 students are selected to attend the IMO training camp and to participate in the third (team-selection) round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming convention of rounds
rubrics_metrics.description: In Iran, the preliminary, first, second, and third round are normally called first, second, third, and fourth round or team selection exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locally the rounds may be referenced as first–fourth rounds; the final round is often called the team selection exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training program structure for team selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The IMO team is selected during the training program which consists of two phases: theoretical part (at fall or winter), which ends with a final course exam, and problem solving part (at early spring), during which the third round of the MO is held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 1 (theoretical) runs in fall/winter and culminates in a course exam; Phase 2 (problem solving) runs in early spring and includes the national team-selection round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception / historical variation in selection procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: In 1996 the team was selected through the second round which consisted of two exams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection procedures can vary year to year; the 1996 example shows the team can be selected at different rounds if the structure is altered (e.g., second round having two exams).

rubrics_metrics.name: Available problem set size
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of available problems is 176.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This page's archive/collection contains 176 problems from the Iran MO across listed years.
